answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it can earn reputation; a randomly selected set of established peers then reviews its work, and a proven lie burns the deposit and lowers the reviewers’ standing too. Spinning up a thousand identities therefore does not create a thousand cheap votes: the attacker must immobilize capital in every account and risk losing it. Even at dawn, a gale of saffron-colored profiles cannot cheaply outweigh costly, accountable endorsements.
